  - 'heading "AI Mode Conversation: How can I help my child give longer, meaningful answers?" [level=1]'
  - heading "How can I help my child give longer, meaningful answers?" [level=2]
  - text: To help your child move past one-word responses and give longer, meaningful answers, you need to
  - mark:
    - text: shift from
    - strong: quizzing them to connecting with them
  - text: . When parents ask consecutive factual questions, children often feel "tested" and shut down with quick answers.
  - link "www.etonhouse.edu.sg":
    - /url: /goto?url=CAESoAEB6zswFRrRkhLfPngnt8Q5g33nEgBvVgrQsNcLwklPUJ0zkcHonbTSck88nAj_qg4Y7cS1Uxedm3pPX2scDtKjmJ_oqbiO11BMftJz6W9gwc6QwBbkT-I1Ks_jsc94hcFY2oUL0Eezq2jwfqgOUVM6eY61TJTr6GULWBip7ra2X-wpOfTlgaccRNHz3IsrUOJbmqDrgeK9vZjE1tHVJecx
  - button "www.etonhouse.edu.sg - Related results":
    - generic: www.etonhouse.edu.sg
  - generic: "You can expand their conversational skills through targeted changes in how you ask, listen, and model communication:"
  - heading "1. Stop Quizzing, Start Narrating" [level=3]
  - text: Instead of asking direct questions where you already know the answer (e.g.,
  - emphasis: "\"What did you do at school today?\""
  - text: ), make observations or narrator statements. This removes the pressure to perform and invites a story.
  - link "YouTube · SaLT by the Sea":
    - /url: /goto?url=CAESYwHrOzAVQBuZ72QdSVfKYchIrccNxXVh6tYKd5z6pRyjSweAusbOe51HlqCLvf0vdRARzZ7ExikP_YZzhR6m4JlyUu4eI3WoJu8uGXgiwm8jnwf2WK-48vlpgDZjzwjJaKpSLg

  - list:

    - strong: "Don't say:"
    - text: "\"Did you have fun at recess?\""
    - strong: "Say:"
    - text: "\"You have a huge smile on your face! It looks like you had an awesome recess.\""
    - text: ❌
    - strong: "Don't say:"
    - text: "\"What is that you drew?\""
    - strong: "Say:"
    - text: "\"Look at all those bright colors you chose for this drawing.\""

  - heading "2. Ask \"Inside\" Questions Rather Than \"Outside\" Questions" [level=3]
  - text: "\"Outside\" questions focus on external facts (what they ate, what grade they got), which yield short answers. \"Inside\" questions target their internal world—their feelings, ideas, and opinions."
  - link "Facebook · Alma's Way":
    - /url: /goto?url=CAESywEB6zswFQ5l1yWL1ZPX7Q4mKAxvqCPAi2TbaxPeOLlRR19JZ_1Bmm1bbcrCTGHF7B5TFKVARjHyg2Ad9snBlDRR59F0rfGLnwth_xuwIYdkl1ziq5C_CJgZ6Xsf1OrW239IFDTq9J-dOgr35ot9hjbdEeI3mXeLxE2WfbnsQ2lPtuhZ5dQTbc__b3HGO1av__wD9DLe2GF0IgSGkiuJG0Kn6T9ZW13oOdgTqNfBT2URKwtBsfQplyTB8xfTc0ielouHUtwq5yFL968rUA

    - strong: "\"What was the hardest part of your day today?\""
    - text: (Often where the real story lives).
    - strong: "\"If you had a magic wand today, what is one thing you would have changed about school?\""
    - strong: "\"Who did you see do something really kind or funny today?\""

  - heading "3. Use the \"Add-On\" Expansion Strategy" [level=3]
  - text: When your child
  - emphasis: does
  - text: give a short response, validate it and model how to lengthen it by adding exactly
  - strong: one or two more details
  - text: .
  - link "YouTube · Carrie Clark, Speech and Language Kids":

  - heading "4. Master the \"Awkward Pause\"" [level=3]
  - text: Children require significantly more time than adults to process language, organize thoughts, and physically form sentences. When you ask a question,
  - strong: wait a full 5 to 10 seconds
  - text: before jumping in. If you rush to fill the silence or restate the question, you interrupt their internal processing and teach them that if they wait long enough, you will do the talking for them.
  - link "The 74":
    - /url: /goto?url=CAESqwEB6zswFfVzm6UTnAGUcof1WOxAXJY8ILtBd53tQzmMiq3vtpZUKa9__DaZ3Gy7AKaWrFDgkqvTYbQEXF0QkPkIrRnwBTk2zLHw5flSOK1HmB4K5Xmq_LryrYWT4Th3iP75V4rqhMU-ct9YHFqWvuUa5LAyjbHA6M88yLkPAGAMEuTGd__DyOocTngeFfNKGqY59cQu_QExPPlBt5_4vSQJqI_LPLky0LIGs7E
  - button "The 74 (+1) - Related results":

    - generic: "+1"
  - heading "5. Model Vulnerability First" [level=3]
  - text: Children learn conversational stamina by listening to you. If you want them to share meaningful details, you must share yours first.
  - link "National Fragile X Foundation":
    - /url: /goto?url=CAESdgHrOzAVB5S-Z_HoYk_rpNe4iTNYor-QGjQk9goRD4FG-iCn_QApATPgRfFmzlJ-AaSCWlyDeYGDAMLFRORpP2EPCGhn7Qo1sMB3PAGoqCR-6GCmKPNUoDrqu5u_3jSueKAdBfnjgWAJXbIq9XUIRj2LgBm2r-0
